guard_streams.source: Ofcom companies must tell customers about their best deals

facts.detail: Providers must warn customers between 10 and 40 days before the minimum contract ends.
The notification must state when the current contract ends.
The notification must show what the customer has been paying and what they will pay after the contract ends.
The notification must include any leaving notice period and the provider's best deals, including relevant new-customer prices.

guard_streams.write_limit: End-of-contract information is a consumer-protection record and not parcel service evidence.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom companies must tell customers about their best deals; Ofcom General Conditions of Entitlement

facts.detail: Customers who remain out of contract must be reminded at least annually and told about the provider's best deals.
The notification rules cover relevant phone, broadband, mobile and pay-TV services.
The framework covers residential and qualifying business customers.
General Condition C1 includes contract duration, renewal, end-of-contract information, annual best-tariff information, switching and termination rights.

guard_streams.write_limit: Contract-status and tariff rights cannot establish exact address availability.

facts.detail: Calls to 03 numbers must cost no more than national-rate calls to 01 or 02 numbers.
03 calls must count toward inclusive minutes in the same way as 01 and 02 calls.
The pricing rules apply across mobile, fixed-line and payphone calls.
Revenue sharing with the called organisation is not allowed for 03 calls.

guard_streams.write_limit: Telephone-number pricing does not prove broadband or mobile coverage at a parcel.

facts.detail: Calls to 0800 and 0808 numbers are free from consumer landlines and mobile phones.
The price of calling 084 numbers is split into an access charge and a service charge.
The service charge must be clearly displayed wherever an 084 service number is advertised or promoted.
The access-plus-service-charge framework applies to 084, 087, 09 and 118 service numbers, not ordinary 01, 02, 03 or mobile 07 calls.

guard_streams.write_limit: Call-cost categories and advertised charges are not network-coverage measurements.

facts.detail: Mobile providers must publish roaming charges on their websites.
On entering another country, providers must normally send an automatic message explaining charges or usage limits.
Where a bill limit is set, the provider must notify the customer when the limit is likely to be reached.
A provider may charge beyond the bill limit only where the customer agrees.

guard_streams.write_limit: Roaming disclosures and bill limits do not establish parcel coverage.

facts.detail: Turning off data roaming can help prevent unintended mobile-data charges abroad.
Using suitable Wi-Fi can reduce roaming data use for maps, email and social media.
Providers must explain how to prevent accidental roaming near borders and help limit costs while the customer is in the UK.
At sea, a device may connect to a ship satellite service whose charges can be higher than normal roaming.

guard_streams.write_limit: Travel-cost controls and network-selection advice cannot populate parcel service fields.

facts.detail: Providers must ensure supplied billing information is up to date and reflects current usage and expenditure.
Providers must notify customers when a service included in the tariff plan has been fully used.
The usage notification must include information about charges incurred outside the tariff plan.
Device or provider apps can track usage but may not always identify which voice minutes are included in the allowance.

guard_streams.write_limit: Usage and billing information is account evidence, not exact parcel connectivity evidence.

guard_streams.source: BDUK Buckinghamshire Hertfordshire and East Berkshire contract

facts.detail: The original CityFibre contract covered around 34,000 premises for £58 million and was signed in January 2024.
The May 2026 redesign revised scope to around 6,000 premises backed by £24.4 million.
The redesign followed expanded commercial rollout and changing market conditions to reduce overlap.
Detailed planning and physical build precede access, and the premise list remains subject to technical change.

guard_streams.write_limit: A redesigned regional contract cannot prove exact current parcel orderability.

guard_streams.source: BDUK Bedfordshire Northamptonshire and Milton Keynes contract

facts.detail: The original CityFibre contract covered around 25,000 premises for £51 million and was signed in February 2024.
The May 2026 redesign revised scope to around 6,000 premises backed by £19.8 million.
The redesign focuses public funding on premises outside expanded commercial plans.
Preparatory construction is required before service access and contract scope can change.

guard_streams.write_limit: Contract values and redesign scope are procurement evidence, not parcel coverage.

facts.detail: Gigaclear was awarded two Project Gigabit contracts for North and South Oxfordshire.
The combined contract value is £26.5 million.
The two contracts target around 10,000 hard-to-reach premises.
The contracts were signed in November 2023 and require detailed planning and physical build before access.

guard_streams.write_limit: Two-contract regional scope does not establish live service at individual parcels.

facts.detail: The Scottish Government is the contracting authority for the North East Scotland regional contract.
GoFibre is the awarded broadband provider.
The contract targets around 63,000 premises across North East Scotland.
The GOV.UK guidance page was published on 15 July 2025 and directs users to Scottish Government detail.

guard_streams.write_limit: Authority, supplier and regional scope do not prove parcel-level availability.

facts.detail: Connect Fibre is the awarded supplier for Derbyshire.
The contract value is £33 million.
The award targets more than 17,000 hard-to-reach premises.
The contract was signed in November 2023, with first access anticipated in 2025 after planning and build.

guard_streams.write_limit: Award and anticipated access information cannot establish parcel completion.

facts.detail: Wildanet will not complete the southwest and central Cornwall contracts in full.
The update records around 13,200 premises covered under the two contracts to date.
Wildanet will not deliver the remaining 7,700 contracted premises.
BDUK states it is moving to arrange alternative supplier plans for affected premises.

guard_streams.write_limit: Partial contract delivery and withdrawal do not identify which exact parcels are served.

facts.detail: The July table records Bedfordshire, Northamptonshire and Milton Keynes at 5,890 contracted and 4,820 built premises.
Buckinghamshire, Hertfordshire and East Berkshire is recorded at 6,090 contracted and 4,050 built.
North Oxfordshire is recorded at 4,180 contracted and 3,860 built premises.
South Oxfordshire is recorded at 5,120 contracted and 3,200 built premises.

guard_streams.write_limit: Rounded, lagged management snapshots cannot identify delivered parcel rows.
